Integration compatibility note from the FlashInfer linear-attention work, checked against this PR at `b24029d`.

The additive default helps the GDN integration, but removing `qk_l2norm_additive_epsilon` needs coordination with the existing KDA callers:

- Merged FE #1418 added that graph attribute, and [FI #6078](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6078) forwards it. [FI #6187](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6187) explicitly passes `1e-6` when auto substitutes cuDNN for the native small-BH route. With this PR's graph schema, those calls get an unexpected-argument `TypeError`: explicit cuDNN fails, while auto falls back to native. Caching unsupported builds prevents repeated build work but does not restore the cuDNN route.
- FI currently has two native KDA normalization contracts: small-BH uses `x * rsqrt(sum_sq + 1e-6)`; the general CuTe/BT16 path uses `x * rsqrt(max(sum_sq, 1e-24))`. Our auto integration preserves the contract of the native route being replaced. Simply dropping the attribute would therefore fix the additive call's argument error but silently change the clamp route's mathematics. Zero/tiny-row coverage matters here; this is distinct from acceptable fusion/reduction rounding differences.
- For GDN, [FI #6186](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6186) currently normalizes Q/K externally with additive `1e-6`, rounds to input dtype, and passes `use_qk_l2norm=False` to FE. This PR's shared FE normalization helper appears to provide the needed formula and dtype boundary. After numerical/performance qualification, FI can pass raw Q/K with `use_qk_l2norm=True` and remove its external normalization. GDN still launches FE's separate normalization kernel/workspace before its attention chain; this is not yet fusion into the GDN attention kernel.

Could we retain compatibility for the existing epsilon argument and an explicit way to request the needed normalization semantics, or coordinate the FI migration before removing/changing them? FE 1.31 version gating alone cannot distinguish these two source contracts. Please also retain equivalent zero/tiny-vector, output/final-state and continuation coverage when replacing the dedicated additive-normalization tests.

This is a source-level integration check; I have not run this PR's kernels.

Finishing the review that was already underway when this merged: **the normalization follow-up needs to cover CAKE as well as the [default Hopper route already reported by Vedaanta](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1454#discussion_r4210866241).** I verified the affected code is unchanged in merged commit `db85ff42`.

Independent SM100 check, BF16, K=V=128, two heads, 32 tokens, safe gates, nonzero initial state and checkpoint cadence 16:

| Q/K amplitude multiplier | CAKE final-state relative RMS vs additive reference | CAKE vs clamp reference | FROST vs additive reference |

| 1 | 0.00471 | 0.00471 | 0.00301 |
| 1e-4 | 0.335 | 0.00439 | 0.00266 |
| 1e-5 | 7.90 | 0.00443 | 0.00256 |

Both references use the same inputs and FP64 recurrent math; only Q/K normalization differs. These comparisons check **final state**, avoiding CAKE's previously documented token-output discrepancy. Its frozen forward body still uses `rsqrt(max(sum_sq, 1e-12))`, whereas this PR makes the graph contract additive `1e-6`. CAKE is opt-in, so this additional case has narrower exposure than the default Hopper finding. Please update/regenerate that route too, or decline incompatible plans until it implements the common contract.

The same three cases on base `b8e39555` all match the old clamp contract for both engines (relative RMS below 0.005). Thus the new cross-provider mismatch is reproducible separately from the pre-existing CAKE output limitation.

Separately, **60 FROST normalization/partial-chunk tests passed** on native SM100, covering forward/backward and grouped heads across all four families. The [FlashInfer argument/normalization compatibility note](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/1454#issuecomment-6044734550) also remains applicable; removing the argument at the caller is insufficient for a caller that requires clamp semantics.

These are follow-up fixes after merge. I did not repeat the H100 or performance measurements in the earlier review, and have not counted the pending CI run as passing.

-# KDA graph Q/K normalization
-
-`graph.kda(..., use_qk_l2norm=True)` retains its existing normalization:
-
-```text
-x * rsqrt(max(sum(x * x), 1e-24))
-```
-
-The optional, append-only `qk_l2norm_additive_epsilon` attribute selects additive
-normalization instead. For example:
-
-```python
-graph.kda(
-    q=q, k=k, v=v, g=g, beta=beta, cu_seqlens=cu_seqlens,
-    use_qk_l2norm=True,
-    qk_l2norm_additive_epsilon=1e-6,
-)
-```
-
-This computes `x * rsqrt(sum(x * x) + epsilon)` in FP32 within the KDA kernel,
-without allocating normalized tensors or submitting separate normalization
-kernels. The normalized values remain in FP32 through the subsequent gate
-scaling, without an intermediate FP16/BF16 rounding step. Reduction and
-rounding order can differ from a separately materialized normalization, so
-bitwise agreement is not promised.
-The attention scale is applied by KDA after normalization, as before.
-
-`None` preserves the original behavior, including its fused rounding order.
-A supplied epsilon must be a finite positive normal FP32 value and requires
-`use_qk_l2norm=True`. This is a numerical operation attribute, not a tuning knob;
-it participates in the graph and kernel compile contracts.
-
-The initial implementation supports the SM100-family FROST KDA **forward graph**
-paths, including chain, uncut and value-dimension split schedules. Other engines
-explicitly decline the attribute. The Torch autograd API, backward graph API and
-standalone summary API do not expose it yet; training requires a matching
-normalization derivative and checkpoint semantics. Existing state ownership,
-workspace, stream and execution contracts are unchanged.
